routes.title: Current Coax and a local C boundary
routes.scope: Run current strings, explicit error results and shared source identities, then call emitted Coax from C through a local-file/protobuf workflow. The capstone checks stale completion, failure and timeout paths in C debug and optimized builds.
limitations: Selected current-language examples do not qualify every Coax feature or chapter. Generic constraints, ownership and other targets retain their own evidence.
The file effect is temporary and local. Decoded protobuf bytes do not authorize a HUD action. General fallible foreign results and asynchronous ownership remain separate completion work.
Teaching examples do not record new product adoption or qualify an app, browser, deployment or full compiler.

prerequisites.compiler: An existing Coax executable with native C emission, supplied with --coax. Receipts bind its actual bytes and options; the runner does not build it.
prerequisites.hardware: CPU terminal; retained observations are Apple silicon/macOS. Another host requires its own matching receipt. No GPU or browser is required.

routes.title: Aethyr fixed steps, input and replay
routes.scope: Run CPU engine-core examples for fixed-step scheduling at four frame rates, one queued press consumed once, and a recorded walk replayed to the same digest with an identified planted divergence.
limitations: The small teaching session does not qualify a rendered or playable full realm, general rigid-body simulation or Forge artifacts.
Browser/Wasm parity belongs to a separate retained harness. This CPU route starts no server, WebGPU page or audio playback.
Existing component consumers such as verse/gridwalk.coax keep their recorded adoption scope. These examples neither migrate a whole realm nor add an adopted_by relationship.

routes.title: Train and resume a tiny module, then inspect MLP and CNN models
routes.scope: Actually train the existing 76-parameter public module for 400 tiny SGD steps, compare every loss and saved float with its reference loop, and resume from step 200. Then construct the public 3322-parameter MLP and 2910-parameter CNN, execute synthetic zero-model gradients and demonstrate atomic refusal of unrepresentable compute weights.
limitations: Only the tiny fixed module is trained here. The MLP and CNN steps are dataset-free API/refusal examples and do not rerun the frozen MNIST learning experiments.
Retained MLP/CNN quality, independent gradients, replay and export records remain separate. Exact example output does not requalify those experiments on this compiler or host.

Convolution is CPU f32 NCHW/OIHW valid stride one with formal first-order f64 tape derivatives. GPU convolution, compiled convolution backward, higher-order transforms, pooling and broader architecture acceptance remain outside this route.
Examples do not count as product adoption. The native mnist-experiment.coax and cnn-experiment.coax consumers retain separate workload and quality gates.

routes.title: Sign and verify an event, then replay a client connection
routes.scope: Sign a complete event with a published BIP-340 test key, verify its ID/signature and altered-field refusals, then drive the pure client connection through scripted handshakes, reconnects, verified events, duplicate/stale reports, acknowledgments and shutdown.
limitations: Signing material is a committed public test vector. No user key, Keychain, wallet, entropy source or external signer is opened.

Transport bytes and times are scripted in memory. No socket is opened or relay contacted; native TLS, browser secret handling, durable storage, live interoperability and deployed relays are separate profiles.
The Pylon consumes the shared signer and relay state machine through its own real transport and admission paths. This offline route does not establish that consumer or production relay readiness.
